title: Lead-cooled fast reactor coolant chemistry
bottleneck: Lead-cooled fast reactors promise passive safety and high temperatures, but liquid lead corrodes steels by dissolving alloying elements, and oxygen control, the key corrosion mitigation, must be maintained precisely in a radioactive, high-temperature loop. Lead also produces polonium-210, an intensely radioactive alpha emitter that complicates maintenance and accidents. Russia operates lead-bismuth naval reactors, but commercial-scale lead coolant experience is thin. Oxygen sensors that work reliably in liquid lead at 500 degrees Celsius are themselves a research problem, making chemistry control hard to verify.
why_it_blocks: Coolant chemistry is the gating science for lead-cooled reactors. Without decades-validated corrosion control, the design cannot be licensed or financed.
current_state: Russia's BREST program and European ALFRED pursue lead cooling. Long-term corrosion data under irradiation remains limited.
